\title{Grounded Continual Learning for Deployed Code LLMs:\\A Verified-Reward Environment with Safe, Gated Weight Updates}

\begin{abstract}
Deployed LLMs are frozen after alignment, discarding the richest stream of task-level experience the model will ever see. We introduce a \emph{grounded continual learning} environment in which a compact code model learns \emph{while serving}, framed as a lifelong Markov Decision Process (MDP) with a factored action space: (i) produce a program for the current task; (ii) choose a \emph{learning operation} (ignore, store, update a LoRA adapter, consolidate, or request review). Every reward is \emph{verified} by sandboxed compilation and unit-test execution --- no learned reward model. Every weight update performs real backpropagation through a frozen base into a low-rank adapter and must clear a \emph{holdout-veto safety gate} before the served weights are swapped (snapshot $\to$ update $\to$ gate $\to$ keep/rollback). We evaluate five continual policies (frozen, always-update, experience replay, online EWC, and a learned contextual-bandit controller) on a drift-injected MBPP stream with measured catastrophic forgetting, backward/forward transfer (BWT/FWT), and a cost-normalized stability--plasticity frontier. The pipeline is single-command reproducible and emits its tables/figures from \texttt{metrics.json}.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
Continual learning, large language models, program synthesis, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, safe deployment, option-control.
\end{IEEEkeywords}

\section{Introduction}
The deployment paradox: a code model receives its densest domain signal \emph{after} it is frozen. Program synthesis is the ideal probe for lifelong learning because correctness is \emph{verifiable} --- compilation and unit tests give objective, deterministic rewards that cannot be gamed by plausible text.

The prior iteration of this project produced a well-tested but unfaithful prototype whose ``LoRA update'' incremented a Python list and whose metrics were hard-coded. Here we commit to a single rule: \emph{every reported number comes from an actually executed gradient update and an actually executed unit test}. This paper reports that rebuilt environment and its first credible empirical signal.

\subsection{Contributions}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Grounded continual MDP.} A lifelong environment for deployed code LLMs with a factored task/learning action space and execution-grounded reward, plus drift injectors that make forgetting \emph{measurable}.
\item \textbf{Safe gated updates.} A snapshot/gate/rollback mechanism (zero-copy via PEFT state-dict) that performs real learning while blocking deployment of adapters that regress a holdout set.
\item \textbf{Cost-aware controller.} A contextual-bandit option-policy over learning operations, which prices compute and forgetting directly into its reward.
\item \textbf{Reproducible harness.} A single command runs the full experiment and regenerates all tables/figures from raw trajectories.
\end{itemize}

\section{Environment and Formalism}
\subsection{Lifelong MDP}
State $s_t=(e_t, \text{mem}, \text{adapters}, \text{perf})$; action $a_t=(a_{\text{task}}, a_{\text{learn}})$. The task action is a program; the learning action is one of $\{\textsc{ignore}, \textsc{store}, \textsc{update\_lora}(r), \textsc{consolidate}, \textsc{review}\}$. Reward $r_t \in [0,1]$ is verified: $r_t = w_{\text{exec}} S_{\text{exec}} + w_{\text{test}}\cdot\text{pass\_rate} + w_q\cdot q(\text{code}) - w_s\cdot\text{violation}$, where $q$ penalizes degenerate solutions (return-a-literal) that otherwise game printed tests.

\subsection{Real gated weight updates}
An \textsc{update\_lora} operation performs PEFT adapter training on $K$ verified trajectories, then the safety gate:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Snapshot adapter tensors via \texttt{get\_peft\_model\_state\_dict}.
\item Score frozen base on a private holdout suite, then the candidate adapter.
\item If $\text{holdout}_{\text{cand}} \ge \text{holdout}_{\text{base}} - \epsilon$, register the adapter (content hash + parent), else rollback and count a rollback.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Metrics}
After a full stream walk we evaluate a frozen policy on every family to form the matrix $R_{i,j}$. We report ACC (final average), BWT (final minus first-contact), FWT (first-contact minus zero-shot), Forgetting, AUC over the stream, stability, and a cost-normalized frontier $\text{ACC} - \lambda\,\text{Forgetting}$.

\section{Experimental Setup}
Model: \texttt{\modelName} ($16$ GB RTX 4060 Ti, bf16). LoRA rank \loraRank, update cap \maxUpdates, gate $\epsilon=0.05$. Stream anti-contamination check: holdout/train overlap $=$ \canaryOverlap\ (\canaryClean). All figures derive from \texttt{metrics.json}.

\section{Discussion}
The structure we target: (a) $\text{forgetting}(\text{always}) > \text{forgetting}(\text{replay}) \simeq \text{forgetting}(\text{ewc})$, proving the stability mechanisms act in weight space; (b) the controller reaches the best cost-normalized frontier, (c) safety-gate rollbacks are non-zero and reduce with replay/EWC. Negative control: under no real update the forgetting rows collapse to noise; positive control: always-update on the drifted family reveals measurable backward interference.

\section{Related Work}
Continual learning (EWC, replay) long studied in vision; LoRA/QLoRA for parameter-efficient updates; vLLM-style serving with runtime LoRA hot-swap for deployment. Our emphasis: verified execution rewards plus a \emph{gated, rollback-capable} update path and an option-level controller.
